doc.title: Shelly Berg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Upcoming projects and balancing the hats
summary: Berg lists television, Korean film, Japanese rock, an opera singer album, a Norway jazz cruise and his own CDs, and the difficulty of balance.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What’s on the docket for you in the very near future? Writing assignments?

Yeah, I’m doing some writing. I just wrapped up a couple of cool television projects. We did the Dennis Miller Millennium Special which was a blast. I did a Korean movie. So © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

you never know what the phone’s going to ring, and so I’ve got some more of the Japanese rock things to do and I’m doing a project with an opera singer who wants to do an orchestral album of songs. So it’s just — if the door’s open, interesting things come in. But I don’t really gauge my life on the writing projects. To me it’s what’s coming up. I’m getting to play the Norway jazz cruise with my trio, so that’s what’s exciting for me, and I’m going to be working on my next CD this summer and there’s three singers that I work with who are all wonderful who I’m doing CDs with this summer as well. And hopefully Bill Watrous and I will be doing another album soon. So I hope to be in the studio playing lots of jazz over the next six or seven months.
Wow. You must have a couple of different calendars to make sure that you’re in the right place at the right time with the right hat on.

That’s the hardest part. It’s really the hardest part. You don’t want to end up with a feeling that you’re not quite nailing it, not quite taking care of business for the university or for the writing office or for the playing or for the family. So that’s really the hardest part, because I don’t want to disappoint in any of those areas, so I’m constantly trying to figure out that balance.
